newsitem.title: USA: Crescent buys Desert Mountain for $229 million.
newsitem.headline: Crescent buys Desert Mountain for $229 million.

text.p: Crescent Real Estate Equities Co. said Friday it has a definitive agreement to acquire Desert Mountain, an exclusive planned community in Arizona, for about $229 million.
The sellers are a subsidiary of Mobil Land Development Corp. and a company owned by investor Lyle Anderson.
The price includes about $80 million of assumed debt that will be repaid at closing.
Crescent said Anderson will convert his ownership into a new partnership interest and serve as the development and operating manager of the property.

The property includes 8,300 acres in the high Sonoran desert that is zoned for the development of over 4,500 lots, as well as the Desert Mountain Club, a private golf, tennis and fitness club serving over 1,600 members.

Crescent said it will offer Crescent Operating Inc. the opportunity to acquire all the voting stock, representing a 5 percent equity interest, in the corporation that will make the investment in the Desert Mountain assets.
Crescent said it plans to retain a 95 percent non-voting interest in the corporation.
The deal is expected to close in the third quarter.
